<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 5. F# Compile Order Wrong — `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9
```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />   <!-- depends on Domain -->
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />     <!-- defines types used by Services -->
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```
F# requires files to be listed in **dependency order** (depended-upon first). `Services.fs` opens `BrokenOrder.Domain` (line 3 of Services.fs), so `Domain.fs` **must** precede `Services.fs`. This project **will fail to compile** with a "namespace or module not found" error.

**Fix:**
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```
(Note: `fsharp/OrderService/OrderService.fsproj` has the correct order already.)

---

### 6. Redundant `Include` + `Update` Causes CS2002 — `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 22–23
```xml
<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
```
The SDK automatically globs `*.cs` into the `Compile` item. Adding an explicit `Include="Class1.cs"` creates a **duplicate entry**, producing compiler warning CS2002 ("source file specified multiple times"). The `Update` then applies to both copies ambiguously.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` line; use only `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 7. Self-Invoking `<MSBuild>` Task (Publish-on-Build) — `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45
```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```
This re-invokes the **same project** via the `<MSBuild>` task with an extra global property (`_IsPublishing=true`). MSBuild creates a **second project instance** that shares the same `OutputPath` and `IntermediateOutputPath`. Both instances race to write the same files, causing intermittent build failures and double-build overhead.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish in the same project instance, with a guard property:
```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild"
        AfterTargets="Build"
        DependsOnTargets="Publish"
        Condition="'$(_IsPublishing)' != 'true'" />
```

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns, not immediately breaking but problematic)

### 8. Hardcoded Windows Paths — `LibA/LibA.csproj` line 7, `LibB/LibB.csproj` line 7
```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```
These are **absolute Windows paths** that break on Linux/macOS, break for any developer whose machine isn't configured identically, and bypass the standard `bin/` layout that the SDK provides.

**Fix:** Remove these entirely (the SDK default `bin/$(Configuration)/$(TargetFramework)/` is almost always correct), or use a relative path with an MSBuild property:
```xml
<OutputPath>$(RepoRoot)artifacts\bin\LibA\</OutputPath>
```

---

### 9. Analyzer Package Missing `PrivateAssets` — `Directory.Build.props`, line 17
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
```
Without `PrivateAssets="all"`, the analyzer package **leaks to downstream consumers**. Any project that references LibA or LibB will also get StyleCop diagnostics applied, which is almost never intended.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>
```

---

### 10. Direct Assembly Reference Instead of PackageReference — `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 27–29
```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```
This is a legacy `packages.config`-style assembly reference with a hardcoded `HintPath` pointing into a `packages/` folder. This skips NuGet restore, asset selection, and transitive dependency resolution.

**Fix:** Replace with a proper `PackageReference`:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

### 11. Target Without `Inputs`/`Outputs` — `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 32–34
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```
This target has no `Inputs` or `Outputs`, so it **runs on every single build** — including incremental/no-op builds. This breaks incremental build optimization.

**Fix:** If this is truly for diagnostics only, it may be acceptable. Otherwise, add `Inputs`/`Outputs` or `Condition` to prevent unnecessary execution:
```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build"
        Inputs="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)"
        Outputs="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.stamp">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
  <Touch Files="$(IntermediateOutputPath)PrintVersion.stamp" AlwaysCreate="true" />
</Target>
```
